Direction A of 3 - proposal

Register السجل

The faithful direction: brand navy is pinned at primary-900 and used literally as the action colour, the canvas is the brand cream, the semantic colours are close in chroma to the two brand colours that already exist, corners are small and the type is one neutral grotesque running in both scripts. It is the direction that can be described to a client in one sentence without a mood board.

  • primary-900 #0B3C5D brand navy - the action colour, verbatim
  • neutral-50 #FAF7F1 brand cream - the canvas
  • neutral-900 #12263A brand ink - body text
  • neutral-600 #5A6472 brand secondary ink - labels and metadata

Who it suits

Government, ETA e-invoicing and procurement buyers; teams moving off a spreadsheet or off another CRM; any client who judges software by how uneventful it is. It is also the cheapest to ship, because most of it already exists in the brand layer.

What it costs

Safest and therefore least distinctive: low-chroma semantics give you thin differentiation between stages in a pipeline chart, and the design will not impress anyone in a pitch.

Density rows 52px / 38px

Primary scale - derived from #0B3C5D

Eleven steps generated in OKLCH at the navy's own hue (243.9 deg) with one chroma curve, then gamut-mapped into sRGB. #0B3C5D is pinned at primary-900 because that is the step whose lightness it actually occupies - it is not moved to the middle of the scale to look tidy. Same token names in all three directions, different values.

Neutral scale - derived from #FAF7F1

Cream is pinned at neutral-50, which is where its lightness lands (0.977 against Tailwind's 0.985 for gray-50). It is not a stock Tailwind grey: the hue starts at the cream's own 84.6 deg and the ramp is built from there. White is a separate --surface-card token, not a scale step.

Radii and two density levels

Density changes padding first and type size second. In all three directions the Arabic body never drops below 16 px, so the compact level pays for its extra rows out of padding and rules, not out of legibility.

Fonts, licensing and self-hosting

The product is installed per client and must not reach a CDN for anything, so every face below is embedded in this file as base64 TTF and is shipped inside the installation. Formats are unsubsetted here (the honest cost of a no-network sheet); a production build would ship WOFF2 subsets.

FamilyLicenceDeliverySource of the licence claim
IBM Plex Sans ArabicSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-ibm-plex (Debian copyright file records OFL-1.1)
IBM Plex SansSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-ibm-plex (Debian copyright file records OFL-1.1)
IBM Plex MonoSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-ibm-plex (Debian copyright file records OFL-1.1)

Every family named in this sheet is SIL OFL 1.1. That licence allows embedding, redistribution and commercial use, requires the copyright notice and licence text to travel with the font files, and forbids selling the font itself. IBM Plex carries a Reserved Font Name clause: distribute the files unmodified and under their own names.

Proposal, not a decision. This sheet exists so the direction is chosen by looking at it. Nothing here is wired into the product; no file under packages/ was touched. Path: docs/design/specimens/register.html

Rendered with locally embedded fonts only - no network request is made by this page. Full rationale, contrast numbers and licensing: docs/design/rebrand-palette-directions.md
